exposure: Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) rate
cohort: The study included 154,478 HBsAg-positive mother-infant pairs with post-vaccination serologic results from 2002 to 2021 in Korea.
finding: The overall MTCT rate after prophylaxis was 2.3%, and the study found that antiviral use, breastfeeding, and cesarean section, combined with conventional immunoprophylaxis, significantly reduced MTCT rates.
mod_finding: Lower MTCT rates were observed for cesarean section (1.9%) compared to vaginal delivery (2.6%).
